growing_tip.body_text: Cabbage | → Caraflex → Farao → Red Express → 2 rows per bed spaced every 18” (45 cm) on the row → Broccoli, cabbage and cauliflowers are all heavy feeders that require lots of compost, +/-1 inch (5 cm) all across the bed. In rich soils, compost can be replaced with a buried cover crop of leguminous nature, but in both cases, we add nitrogen-rich organic fertilizers like pelleted chicken manure (5-3-2) to help the plant quickly develops its canopy. → A second boost of nitrogen is added to the crop +/- 14 days after the transplant by amending the soil with blood or alfalfa meal. | We plan different successions of cabbages in the spring and later in the summer for fall crops, avoiding plantings in the heat of the summer. We plant cabbages with other heavy feeding crucifers like, broccoli, cauliflowers and kohlrabi, all crops which spend +/- 60 days in the field. → Rotary harrow → Broadfork → 30” bed prep rake + marking tubes → Declumping tray → Anti-insect net and hoops → Remove tarp and-or clean large debris. Use the rake if needed.* → Uniformly apply compost and amendments and pass with the rotary harrow at a depth of 2” (5 cm). To make transplanting easier (seeing as the soil is loose after being harrowed), we only prepare the beds when we are about to transplant. → Using the bed prep rake and 2 tubes, mark the rows both lengthways and sideways. Bring the well-watered trays. → Using the declumping tray to facilitate clump extraction, 1 person will drop the seedling while 2 others transplant the plants as fast as possible. 3 people/100’ bed is a good ratio for efficient workflow. → Bury the seedling all the way to where the leaves start to branch out. → Install the hoops every 5’ (1.5 m) and cover the crops with the anti-insect net. Set sandbags on every hoop. → Install irrigation and water the soil until it is deeply moist. * If the previous crop is too well established, or if the bed is too messy, mow the crop as low as possible and harrow at a depth of 2” (5 cm...

irrigation.body_text: → Drip tape (4 per bed) or sprinkler | → Root depth: Shallow (6”-24”) → Critical period: Head development → General: Needs even moisture or heads might crack 1
